reason: E2 supports the general benefit of two-step precipitation hardening for fine, uniform precipitates in Ti alloys and HEAs, but does not mention Ni3Ti or the specific alloy. E1 and E3 discuss strengthening mechanisms in general terms without evidence for Ni3Ti precipitation in a Ti–Ni primary HEA. No cited evidence demonstrates Ni3Ti formation, coherency, or the specific heat treatment parameters for the proposed composition, leaving most key premises unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: A two-step heat treatment (solutionizing + aging) can produce a fine, uniform dispersion of precipitates in Ti alloys and HEAs.
Ni3Ti precipitates can form in a Ti–Ni-rich HEA matrix and be coherent.
Fine, coherent precipitates impede dislocation motion, increasing yield strength and creep resistance at elevated temperatures.
The proposed Ti30Ni30Cr20Al10V10 alloy can be solution-treated at ~1050 °C and aged at ~600 °C to achieve nanoscale Ni3Ti precipitates without significant coarsening.
The predicted 20–30% strength increase and reduced creep rate at 650–700 °C are achievable based on prior evidence.
